column1: # Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave (Switch 2, update v131072). Plays on the Mac
# Intelligent Systems' engine on NintendoWare (G3d, Ui2d, Vfx, Atk), SDK 22.2.0 built for the Switch 2 (nnSdk-Generic_22_2_0), NVN2 (Ampere shaders, DLSS); modules main + subsdk2 (movie) + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (updates/131072/ only: the update is the whole game) with scripts/pack_dump.py. Movies: AV1 in WebM.
# The display version is unknown: a dump has no control data (docs/reference/services.md, The display version of a game packed from a dump), so the title shows "Ver. ?"
# Not loaded, main takes nothing from them the host does not supply: subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_DLSS: the host serves DLSS itself), subsdk1 (C / libc)
# The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on, and the game sets no heap: its memory comes from StandardAllocator::Initialize(nullptr, 36 GB) in the alias
# region, which the host fits to the region (9.19 GB here). With the 4.375 GB region of a Switch 1 game it had mapped 4.03 GB by its second movie and that movie's buffers failed
# (docs/reference/memory.md, Sizing the pool and alias region for virtual address memory). 256 MB in front + 9.5 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 256 MB heap region: more than an
# iPhone's 6 GB reservation without the extended-virtual-addressing entitlement, so the Mac only for now
# The Switch 2's 9 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure)
# The game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 at startup (the NSP script's address region check saw it): the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
